learn.title: Rooftop Solar & Net Metering in India
learn.intro: Rooftop solar systems transform sunlight into clean electricity for homes and businesses, reducing grid dependence. Net metering policies allow excess power to be fed back into the grid, earning credits. This synergy accelerates India's renewable energy transition while making solar affordable for urban households.
learn.c1_text: Solar panels use photovoltaic cells to convert sunlight into DC electricity. A typical 1kW rooftop system generates 4-5 units daily. Like a water wheel harnessing flow, panels capture sunlight's energy to power lights, fans, and appliances directly or via the grid.
learn.c2_text: Net metering credits surplus solar power fed into the grid. India's policy allows 1:1 export-import ratio up to 100% of installed capacity. Analogous to a bank account, unused credits offset future bills, encouraging investment in solar for residential and commercial users.
learn.c3_text: India's MNRE promotes rooftop solar through subsidies and net metering. Over 90 GW solar capacity installed by 2024, with 6 GW from rooftop systems. States like Gujarat and Tamil Nadu lead in net metering adoption, supporting the national 280 GW renewables target by 2030.
learn.stat3: Net metering credits 1:1 for surplus power
learn.stat4: MNRE supports 100% net metering up to system capacity

learn.title: Solar Inverters: String vs Micro vs Hybrid
learn.intro: Solar inverters convert DC power from panels into usable AC electricity. Understanding string, micro, and hybrid inverters helps optimize system efficiency and cost. This knowledge empowers informed decisions for residential and commercial solar installations.
learn.c1_text: String inverters manage multiple panels in series, converting DC to AC centrally. Efficient for uniform sunlight conditions. Like a single engine powering a train, they simplify maintenance but suffer from single-point failure or shading losses reducing overall output.
learn.c2_text: Microinverters attach to individual panels, optimizing each's output independently. They enhance performance in partial shading or panel failures. Residential systems benefit from 10-15% higher energy yield. Like dedicated engines per car, they improve reliability and monitoring.
learn.c3_text: Hybrid inverters manage solar, battery storage, and grid interaction. They prioritize self-consumption and store excess energy. US DOE notes hybrid systems support 30-50% grid independence. Ideal for homes with solar+battery setups, enabling smart energy management.
learn.stat2: String inverters handle 10-20 panels per unit
learn.stat4: 95% of US solar systems use string inverters
learn.readLabel: Learn at US Dept of Energy

learn.title: Capacity Factor Explained
learn.intro: Capacity factor reveals actual energy output versus theoretical maximum. It highlights real-world performance of renewable systems. Understanding this metric is crucial for investors, policymakers, and planners assessing energy project viability and grid integration potential.
learn.c1_text: Capacity factor = (actual energy output / maximum possible output). A 100 MW solar plant with 25% capacity factor produces 219,000 MWh annually. Like a car's average speed vs top speed, it reflects real-world operational efficiency.
learn.c2_text: Solar capacity factors range 15-25% due to nighttime and weather. Onshore wind achieves 35-45% with consistent winds. Offshore wind reaches 45-55%. These differences influence location selection and energy storage needs for grid stability.
learn.c3_text: US EIA data shows capacity factors guide renewable energy subsidies and grid planning. Lower solar factors require larger installations for equivalent output. Policymakers use this metric to set realistic targets and optimize energy mix for reliability and cost-effectiveness.
learn.readLabel: Read at US Energy Info Admin

learn.title: Flow Batteries for Grid Storage
learn.intro: Flow batteries store energy in liquid electrolytes, offering scalable grid-scale storage. Their long lifespan and rapid response make them ideal for integrating renewables. Understanding vanadium and iron systems unlocks insights into next-generation energy storage solutions.
learn.c1_text: Flow batteries use two liquid electrolytes (vanadium or iron) pumped through cells. Energy stored depends on tank size, not cell type. Like a fuel tank for electricity, they provide long-duration storage (8-12 hours) with minimal degradation over thousands of cycles.
learn.c2_text: Vanadium systems use V+2/V+3/V+4/V+5 states for charge/discharge. Iron-based uses Fe^2+/Fe^3+ with lower cost. Vanadium offers better scalability and efficiency (75-85%), while iron systems are cheaper but less efficient (60-70%). Both suit different grid needs.
learn.c3_text: US DOE highlights flow batteries for renewable integration and peak shaving. Projects like Dalian (China) use vanadium for 100 MWh storage. In India, flow batteries support rural microgrids. Their 20-year lifespan and fire safety make them ideal for utility-scale deployments.
learn.stat2: Flow batteries last 20+ years with minimal degradation
learn.stat3: Iron-based systems cost 50% less than lithium-ion
learn.stat4: Grid-scale flow battery market to reach $1.5B by 2030
learn.readLabel: Explore at US Dept of Energy

learn.title: Green Hydrogen via Electrolysis
learn.intro: Green hydrogen production splits water into hydrogen and oxygen using renewable electricity. PEM and alkaline electrolyzers differ in efficiency, cost, and application. This technology is pivotal for decarbonizing heavy industry, transport, and energy storage globally.
learn.c1_text: Electrolysis uses DC current to split water (2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂). PEM electrolyzers operate at 80°C with high efficiency (70-80%), while alkaline runs at 70-85°C (60-70% efficiency). Like a water-splitting machine, they produce hydrogen for fuel cells or industrial use.
learn.c2_text: PEM systems offer rapid response and high pressure output but cost more ($1,000/kW vs $800/kW for alkaline). Alkaline is mature and cheaper for large-scale projects. PEM suits variable renewable input; alkaline excels in steady-state operations. Both aim to cut hydrogen production costs below $2/kg by 2030.
learn.c3_text: IRENA notes India's National Green Hydrogen Mission targets 5 MT/year production by 2030. Alkaline electrolyzers dominate current projects due to cost. States like Gujarat plan green hydrogen hubs. Renewable integration and scaling production are key to achieving energy independence and export potential.
learn.stat4: India aims for 5 MT/year green hydrogen by 2030

learn.title: Electric Vehicles Explained
learn.intro: Electric vehicles (EVs) transform transportation with zero tailpipe emissions and energy efficiency. Understanding their motors, regenerative braking, and charging infrastructure is vital for accelerating the global shift to sustainable mobility and reducing fossil fuel dependence.
learn.c1_text: EVs use electric motors powered by onboard batteries, delivering instant torque and efficiency. AC induction or permanent magnet synchronous motors convert electrical energy to motion. Like a water wheel driven by electricity, they provide smooth acceleration with 90%+ energy efficiency compared to 20-30% for gasoline engines.
learn.c2_text: Regenerative braking captures kinetic energy during deceleration, converting it back to electricity. This boosts range by 10-20% and extends battery life. Similar to a bicycle dynamo, it reduces wear on friction brakes while recharging the battery, enhancing overall efficiency and sustainability.
learn.c3_text: India's US DOE-supported EV push includes public fast-charging stations. By 2024, over 10,000 EV charging points exist nationwide. Rapid chargers (50 kW) replenish 80% in 30 minutes. Policy incentives and battery swapping aim to address range anxiety, supporting the target of 30% EV sales by 2030.
learn.readLabel: Explore at US Dept of Energy
